title: Inline base64 attachments are gone: the attachments field on Action and the Attachment / AttachmentInput types have been removed
content:
The legacy inline format is not deprecated, it is **removed**. The document records Phase 3 as done: the `attachments` field on `Action` and the inline `AttachmentInput` / `Attachment` types (`{ data: string /* base64 */, mimeType, extension?, fileName? }`) no longer exist, and all attachment data flows through `IAttachmentService`, `IAttachmentStore` and `IAttachmentTransport`.

The problems that motivated the removal are worth keeping, because they are the argument for refs in any similar design: operations carried the full binary payload through the job queue, the sync channels and GraphQL transport; large files bloated the operation store and sync bandwidth permanently, since operations are immutable; an attachment could not be uploaded independently of submitting an action; and there was no lifecycle at all — an attachment either existed inline or did not.

Phase 2 completed the sync half: channels no longer transfer inline attachment data, bytes move via the transport (lazy fetch or eager push), and transport configuration became part of the remote/channel configuration.

For a model author migrating an old schema, the mechanical change is to replace `data: String` (or a composite `{ image, imageMediaType, imageUrl }`) with a single `attachment: AttachmentRef` on both the input and the state type.
